image_prompt.text: A chain of butter-pat platforms spaced to physics-legal jump limits, zigzagging upward as the ordered route through the course, each stage a step harder than the last
Wider flat butter checkpoint pads every 4-5 stages, each with a flag or marker planted in it
Long butter-pat jumps, squishy bounce pads that launch players upward like soft trampolines, and stepping-stone paths of butter across open gaps
Butter slabs sliding back and forth across gaps and rotating platforms turning underfoot
Butter platforms that fade away a moment after being stepped on
Narrow butter walkways and balance beams to cross without losing footing
A large golden finish platform at the top of the climb, dressed as a celebration area
Sloped butter ramps and creamy slides linking platforms between stages
Everything moulded from warm butter — soft, rounded, squishy-looking surfaces in warm yellows (#FFD700, #FFC107, #FFE082), creamy whites and golden accents

layout_placement.text: Respawn set on each checkpoint pad every 4-5 stages, so a fall returns the player to the last cleared stage instead of the bottom of the climb
End-of-course reward area on the finish platform where players who top out collect the payoff

notes: Preset Classic Obby kept, with its shape swapped from course-flat to course-terraced because the prompt asks for a zigzagging ascent into a tall vertical obby; all four preset options (path-track, checkpoint-respawn, obstacle-jump, obstacle-moving) retained and quoted route is the terraced shape's.

Close shape call: 'zigzag upward' was read as switchback terraces with clear air above each platform (P6 + tiered) rather than course-tower, which would stack platforms directly over each other and force P2. P2 is not ready, and the prompt never asks for a wrapped or spiral tower — flag if a true stacked tower was intended.

Prompt requests configurable attributes (StageCount default 24, Difficulty, Squishiness, ButterColor, PlatformSpacing, IncludeCheckpoints, MovingPlatformSpeed, DisappearingDelay). These are behaviour and tuning parameters the layout handoff cannot carry; StageCount is preserved as the count on path-track.

'Narrow walkways and balance beams' promoted to obstacle-climb, which is where the tightrope-style traverse lives in this genre; nothing in the prompt is contact-lethal, so hazard-kill was deliberately not taken.

would have asked: Sounds like a classic difficulty-chart obby: a 20-plus stage platform track that gets harder as it goes, wider checkpoint pads with flags every few stages, sliding and rotating platforms, platforms that vanish under you, bouncy launch pads, narrow beams, ramps and slides, and a big finish platform — all of it moulded out of butter, and built climbing in a zigzag rather than flat across the ground. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: whether the zigzag ascent is meant to wrap so platforms sit directly above each other, which needs overhanging surfaces and is not a route we can build today; built as switchback terraces instead, and I would have offered to note the tower version for when that route lands.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
